claims.claim: 'Nunc mihi scribenti nuntius supervenit, narrans mihi navem parari qua invitus vehar in meam regionem ... Si in mare projiciar more Jonae, qui et ipse in Hebraeo Columba dicitur, orate ut vice ceti sit quidam felici revocans remigio tutus celator, qui Jonam vestrum terrae reddat optatae'
claims.witness: Columbanus, Letter IV to his monks, PL80 l.21305-21326 (OCR 'Nune', 'Jona', 'Hebrieo', 'celi', 'terra red-/dat optatz:e'); placed at Nantes by Mabillon, as Gallandi quotes him (PL80 l.16362-16370, 16380-16382); the letter says 'hic in vicinia Brittonum' (l.21345)

claims.claim: Jonas places him at Nantes, where Bishop Suffronius and Count Theudebald prepared to send him to Ireland by the king's order
claims.witness: Jonas, Life ch. 45-47, tr. Munro (jonas munro1895 l.1282, 1330-1332)

claims.claim: 'Columban, who is also called Columba, was born on the island of Ireland'; his birthplace 'called by the inhabitants, Lagener-land', glossed by Munro 'Leinster, in Ireland'
claims.witness: Jonas, Life ch. 6 and 9, tr. Munro (jonas munro1895 l.109-110, 220-221, 235; 'Lagen-/er-land' runs over a line break)

claims.claim: Jonas wrote after Columbanus's death and names informants: 'Theudegisil himself told us of this', 'we have learned from Chamnoald ... who was his attendant and disciple', 'We learned this from Eustasius'
claims.witness: Jonas, Life ch. 23, 30, 54 (jonas munro1895 l.708-709, 864-866, 1530-1531; OCR 'Btis' for 'his' at l.865)

claims.claim: Munro: 'Jonas, the author of this life, became a monk at Bobbio, in northern Italy, three years after Columban's death', and obtained material 'as he himself said, from the stories told by the saint's companions'
claims.witness: Munro's introduction (jonas munro1895 l.76-79); Jonas's preface, which Munro says he omitted (l.96-98), is not held in this file

claims.claim: Jonas's preface: about three years before, at the brothers' urging and Abbot Bertulf's command, he promised to write the deeds of 'almi patris Columbani', since many who saw them are still alive 'qui nobis non audita sed visa narrent', and he learned more 'per venerabiles viros Attalam et Eustasium', successors at Bobbio and Luxeuil
claims.witness: Jonas, preface, in Barralis 1613 from Surius (barralis_chronologia-sanctorum-insulae-lerinensis-lat_1613 l.36424-36436; poor OCR, e.g. 'Benulphi', 'Eutiachium' for Eustasium; the Library header asks that the scan be checked before quoting); Surius's heading calls Jonas 'eius aequali' (l.36418-36419)

claims.claim: Jonas calls Brunhild 'a second Jezebel' and has Theuderic's line destroyed within three years as Columbanus foretold
He studied under Sinell, then entered 'the monastery of Bangor', under 'the holy Congall'; after many years he longed 'to go into strange lands' and left with twelve companions
Jonas's text: 'he started out in the twentieth year of his life'; Munro's note: 'More probably, thirtieth. The manuscripts differ.' Gallandi: 'aetatis annum tunc agens tricesimum'
claims.witness: jonas munro1895 l.278-285; Gallandi's prolegomenon, PL80 l.16145-16146

claims.claim: He settled in the Vosges wilderness at Anagrates (Anegray), then built Luxeuil and Fontaines and 'established the rule which they were to follow'
Rule, ch. III: 'Ergo quotidie jejunandum est, sicut quotidie orandum est, quotidie laborandum, quotidieque est legendum'
Penitential: 'Diversitas culparum diversitatem facit poenitentiarum: nam et corporum medici diversis medicamenta generibus componunt: aliter enim vulnera, aliter morbos ...'
claims.witness: Poenitentiale Columbani B, wasserschleben1851 l.22218-22221 (OCR 'D.versilas', 'eorporum'); also PL80 l.17714-17717

claims.claim: Wasserschleben: the penitential was published by Fleming in 1667 from a Bobbio codex, and was 'unzweifelhaft nicht in Irland, sondern auf dem Kontinent ... entweder in Burgund ... oder in Oberitalien abgefasst'
claims.witness: Wasserschleben's introduction, wasserschleben1851 l.1559-1569 (OCR 'Co lumban', 'Fl cm m in g')

claims.claim: He rebuked Theuderic for concubines; Brunhild brought him Theuderic's sons; 'Know that these boys will never bear the royal sceptre, for they were begotten in sin'
Barmby: Columbanus 'had already given offence in Gaul ... by his continuing to observe and uphold the custom of his own Celtic Church with regard to the time for keeping Easter'
claims.witness: Barmby's note to Gregory, Register IX.127 (npnf213 l.4182-4190)

claims.claim: To Gregory: 'error is manifestly ancient; but truth which reproves it is ever more ancient still'
claims.witness: Columbanus to Pope Gregory, tr. Barmby (npnf213 l.4592-4594); Latin also PL80 Ep. I and Mansi 10

claims.claim: 'So, twenty years after he had come to this place the holy man departed'; escorted to Nantes; the ship stuck until his goods were unloaded; 'all ... understood that God did not wish Columban to return home'
He preached among the Swabians near Bregenz, then went to Italy, 'received with honor by Agilulf, king of the Lombards'

Paul the Deacon: Columban 'came into Italy, and was kindly received by the king of the Langobards, and built a convent in the Cottian Alps which is called Bobium'; 'there was established there a great community of monks'
claims.witness: Paul the Deacon, HL IV.41, tr. Foulke (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.8968-8972, 9008-9011)

claims.claim: 'After a single year in his monastery of Bobbio, Columban the man of God, ended his devout life on the XI. day before the Kalends of December'; Munro: 'November 21st, probably 615'
Gallandi: death on 21 November 615, 'ut post Cointium docet Mabillonius'

To a Gallic synod: 'ut mihi liceat cum vestra pace et charitate in his silvis silere et vivere juxta ossa nostrorum fratrum decem et septem defunctorum, sicut usque nunc licuit nobis inter vos vixisse duodecim annis'; 'Capiat nos simul, oro, Gallia, quos capiet regnum coelorum, si boni simus meriti'
The synod was gathered over him on Easter: 'quod mei causa in unum tanti congregati sunt sancti'; 'pro me de Paschate discutiendo occasio vobis sancta effecta est synodus'
claims.witness: Columbanus, Letter II, PL80 l.20600-20612 (OCR 'Pas-/chate diseutiendo')

claims.claim: Fredegar IV.36 tells the quarrel 'Anno 14 regni Teuderici'; Krusch: 'Hoc caput plerumque ad verbum ex Vita Columbani auctore Iona ... fluxit'; Krusch reckons Theuderic's fourteenth year as 608
claims.witness: fredegar krusch1888 l.10027 (chapter text), 10066-10074 (Krusch's notes 7 and 8) (OCR 'Teudei'ici', 'lona')

claims.claim: Bede, HE II.4: Laurence and his fellow bishops write that 'we have been informed by Bishop Dagan ... and the Abbat Columbanus in France, that the Scots in no way differ from the Britons in their behaviour'

Eustasius defended the Rule of Columbanus against Agrestinus at Mâcon; Mansi heads the council 627 and quotes Jonas's Life of Eustasius; Fabricius: 'Synodum Matisconensem ad annum 627 alii referunt, Mabillonius ... ad annum 624. Cointius ... ad annum 625'
claims.witness: mansi tomus-10 l.61320-61385 (OCR 'Agreftini'); Fabricius's notice, PL80 l.15978-15983

claims.claim: Jonas names houses founded under his rule: Donatus, whom Columbanus raised from the font, bishop of Besançon (Palatium); his brother Ramelen (in the Jura), born of the same promise; Ado and Dado, blessed as children (Munro's note on Ado's: 'The monastery Jouarre near Meaux'; Dado's 'near Brieg, on the little river Rebais')
Jonas: 'If anyone wishes to learn of his activity, let him seek it in the saint's writings'

Gallandi on the sermons: 'Lectu sunt sane dignissimae, ac miram ubique pietatem cum pari eloquio conjunctam spirant'; on the letters: 'omnes fervido zelo praeditae atque libertate Christiana exaratae'

Letters: I to Gregory (Barmby: 'poor dove in Christ'); II to a Gallic synod, III and V to Boniface IV, IV to his monks, signed 'Columba peccator' in II-IV; V signed 'Palumbus'; VI 'Ad quemdam suum discipulum'
Foulke: the Life was 'Written by Jonas, a monk of Bobbio, about 640 (Hodgkin, VI, 105)'; 'St. Columban was born in Leinster, Ireland about 543 ... died at Bobbio, Italy, 615', both citing Hodgkin
claims.witness: Foulke's notes to Paul the Deacon (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15760-15762; also l.8977-8978, 9026); Hodgkin is not held

contested_claims.claim: His age when he left Ireland
sides: Jonas's text as Munro translates it: his twentieth year (jonas munro1895 l.278-279); the Latin Life in Barralis also reads 'vigesimum aetatis annum agens' (barralis l.36689)
Munro: 'More probably, thirtieth. The manuscripts differ' (l.285); Gallandi: his thirtieth (PL80 l.16145-16146)
His poem to Fedolius: 'Nunc ad Olympiadis ter senos venimus annos' (PL80 l.22970; quoted by Gallandi as 'ter senae', l.16163)
Ussher, as Gallandi reports him: seventy-two if four-year Olympiads, ninety if five (PL80 l.16164-16168; OCR 'quadragesimum' at l.16166)
Mabillon, as Gallandi quotes him: five-year Olympiads, 'annos nonaginta' (l.16135, 16178-16181); Goldast's notes: 'Olympias, lustrum, id est, quinque annorum spatium', so about ninety (l.24145-24170)
Gallandi and the Histoire littéraire: seventy-two (l.16181-16186)

contested_claims.claim: Who received him in Gaul, and when he came to Luxeuil
sides: Jonas: King Sigibert, ruling Austrasia and Burgundy (jonas munro1895 l.342-348)
Munro: 'Sigibert died 575, and was king only of Austrasia' (l.377)
Gallandi: Luxeuil founded in Burgundy under Guntram; 'De tempore quo Luxovium accessit haud plane constat'; Le Cointe and Mabillon give 590 (PL80 l.16146-16151)
Benedictine editors, as Barmby reports: the letter to Gregory 598-599 (npnf213 l.4179-4181)
Mabillon, as Gallandi reports: the letter to the Gallic synod 602, the twelfth year in the Vosges (PL80 l.16350-16352)
A note in Mansi 10: not clear whether the twelve years count from his coming to Gaul or to Luxeuil (mansi tomus-10 l.49398-49406)
Gallandi: Letter IV in 610 after Mabillon, Letter V in 615 on the Three Chapters (PL80 l.16380-16384, 16404-16412)
Gallandi: 'in Lagenia, Hiberniae provincia, circa medium saeculi VI ortus traditur' (PL80 l.16138-16139; OCR 'cirea')
Foulke's notes to Paul the Deacon, citing Hodgkin: 'about 543' (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.8977-8978, 15761)

absent_details.note: No ancient line held gives it. Gallandi reports a tradition of about the mid-sixth century (PL80 l.16138-16139); Foulke's 'about 543' cites Hodgkin, who is not held. The scan's 'c.543-615' rests on Foulke's note and on editors' years.
Jonas says he wrote it at Milan (jonas munro1895 l.1644-1648); Fabricius lists the 'Liber contra Arianos' among works that are 'desiderantur' (PL80 l.16099-16112). Not held.

Munro omits the preface (jonas munro1895 l.96-98). The Latin Life with the preface is held in Barralis 1613, copied from Surius, in poor OCR (barralis_chronologia-sanctorum-insulae-lerinensis-lat_1613 l.36414 ff.; e.g. 'vigesimum aetatis annum agens', l.36689). Krusch's MGH SRG 37 edition is not held. Fredegar IV.36 preserves the conflict chapters in Latin.
Gregory of Tours does not name him in the held Arndt-Krusch volume; the Columban entries in Dalton's index point to Dalton's own introduction.

Foulke, citing Hodgkin, gives 'about 640' (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15760); Munro says Jonas came to Bobbio three years after Columbanus's death and was 'soon employed' on the Life (jonas munro1895 l.76-78). The Library header's 'c. 640-642' is a catalogue date. Jonas names Dagobert after Chlotar (jonas munro1895 l.1420-1421) and Babolen as 'now abbot of Bobbio' (l.712-713). The brief says only that Jonas wrote after his death.

Et dixit mihi: Vere, abba Joannes, hodie nibil ultra studea- mus; satis enim edificati sumus' (OCR as in the file: 'Tune' = Tunc, 'perrezimns' = perreximus, 'Dorwit iſle' = Dormit ille, 'ec0s' = eos, 'mortyus', '}1»winus' = dominus); the brief tells it in modern words, the closing words as a modern rendering of the Latin
claims.witness: John Moschus, Spiritual Meadow ch. 77, Latin column (john-moschus pg87-3 l.9983-9993, 10006-10007, 10086-10095)

claims.claim: The third blind man had followed the funeral of a dead man 'optime indutum' and, entering the tomb, 'exui ipsum, nihil ei relinquens preter unum lintes- men'

Dedication 'JOANNIS EVIRATUS DILECTO suo IN CHRISTO, SOPHRONIO SOPHISTR.'; 'Ex his ego flores pucherrimos decerpens, coronam tibi ex immarcescibili ac perenni prato contexui, fidelis- sime fili, eamque libi, ac per te omnibus offero' (OCR 'SOPHISTR.' = SOPHISTAE, 'pucherrimos', 'libi' = tibi); the closing line is a modern rendering of the Latin
claims.witness: Spiritual Meadow, dedication, Latin column (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3756-3757, 3781-3786)

claims.claim: The old notice: 'Primi porro auctoris elogium (quod bona ex parte Photius Bibliothecæ suæ inservit, integreque ex MS. codice Vaticano antiquo a Francisco Oli- varii Latine redditum, Heribertus noster Roswey- dus edidit inter vitas Patrum)'; later called 'prefixum Prato spirituali elogium'
claims.witness: Daniel Papebroch, Life of Sophronius (Acta Sanctorum, March II, p. 65, reprinted by Migne) (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24917-24921, 25462-25463); the Life is Papebroch's by Fabricius's notice, 'Papebrochius in Actis Sanctor. ad 11 Martii tom. II, p. 65 seq.' (l.3521-3522) and Migne's heading (l.24641)

claims.claim: The notice: he renounced the world 'in monasterio saneti Patris nostri Theo- dosii, abbatis et archimandritz omnium, que sunt Hierosolymis, cenobiorum'; lived 'in deserto ad sanctum Jordanem non exiguo tempore'; then 'in Novo, quod dicitur, manasterio, quod a sancto et magno Palre nostro Saba ejusque discipulis eon- structum'; 'audiens qua tyrannide Persæ Romanos oppressissent, oc- casione cedis Mauritii imperatoris ejusque liberorum ... perrexit ad par- tes Antiochiz magne'; then 'Alexandriam se contulit' and went 'nsque ad Oasim'; hearing 'saneta loca fuisse occupata', 'ad magnam Romanorum urbem navigio appulit una cum cha- rissimo diseipulo suo Sopbronio'
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24932-24965); an anonymous notice of unknown date

claims.claim: The notice: he wrote the book 'cum (sun ad Deum migrationis tempus previdis- set'; handed it to Sophronius; asked 'ui reliquias suas ne Rome relinqueret, sed area lignea inclusas ad montem Sinzum transſerre co- naretur', or, if a barbarian tumult prevented it, 'in monasterio 8. Theo- dosii ... ipsas deponi'; at Ascalon the way to Sinai was barred 'propter tyrannicas incur- siones eorum, qui yocantur Agareni'; at Jerusalem 'in S. Theodosii cœmeterio deposuit' (OCR 'sun' = suae, 'area' = arca, 'Sinzum' = Sinaeum)
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25365-25398, 25455-25462)

claims.claim: Papebroch: 'Annum revergionis significat octave indi- clionis character vi cesimum supra $excentesimum ſuisse' (620; OCR 'revergionis')
claims.witness: Papebroch (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25355, 25403-25405, column break between 'indi-' and 'clionis')

claims.claim: Papebroch: Tiberius began to reign 'anno 579 exeunte'; Maurice was killed 'circa finem anni 602'; Moschus reached Rome 'In exitnu erat papz Deus-dedit pontificatus, vel Bonifacii Vinchoatus'
Papebroch: the book was first spread by Sophronius, who had brought it 'a magistro Ro- me, ubi perſectus demum est, moriente, velut testamento acceptum, una cum deſuncti cadavere in Palæstinam'

Fabricius: monastic life 'in conobio 8. Theodosii (e), Hierosolymis et in deserto ad Jordanem et in nova S. Sabe laura'; 'notissimumque illum librum de Vitis monachorum illius etatis usque ad Heraelii 4 tempora fabulosis non destitutum narrationibus, composuit ad Sophronium sophistam, discipulum (/) et itinerum comitem, (deinde patriarcham Hierosolymitanum)'; 'Passim ... invehitur in heresin Severi Acephali'; 'Diem obiisse supremuin a. C. 620, a Joanne Bollando adnotatum reperi'
claims.witness: Notice from Fabricius, Bibliotheca Graeca, ed. Harles, l. X, p. 124, as Migne prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3368-3400; OCR rough). The notice mixes Fabricius's text with Harles's additions (marked 'HAL.'); the sentences cited stand in its first paragraph, before any 'HAL.' mark

claims.claim: Severus is Severus of Antioch, who rejected Chalcedon: 'Severus sedem Antiochenam expulso S. Fla- ano per vim invasit anno 513, ex secta Acepha- lorum'; Severus wrote 'adversus Joannem Cæsa- riensem Grammaticum concilii Chalcedonensis de- ſensorem'
claims.witness: Notes in the same volume (john-moschus pg87-3 l.37983-37985, 5774-5776)

claims.claim: Second Council of Nicaea: 'Stephanus itaque monachus acceptum librum legit : « Ejusdem Pairis nostri Sophronii e Limonario; dixit Theodorus abbas, Xliotes, quod erat quidam inclusus (b); » et cztera. Ubi totum caput 45, quod in hoc libro babetur, ad verbum redditur'; John of Damascus and the synod 'librum Sophronio patriarchæ Hierosolymitano inscribunt'
claims.witness: Aloysius Lipomanus, letter to the reader (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3664-3672)

claims.claim: The year of Nicaea II: 'In Actis synodi septime, sive Nicene secundo (a. C. 787 manu aliquoties laudatur Sophronius. afferunturque loca sub illius nomine' (OCR as in the file)
claims.witness: Notice on Sophronius in the same volume, after 'Hactenus Fabricius' (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24447-24449); whose words (Fabricius's or Harles's) the section is is not marked

claims.claim: Chapter 45: an 'inclusus in monte Olivarum'; the demon: 'Noli adorare bane ima- ginem, et ultra te non impugaabo'; the image 'expres:am ſiguram dominæ nostrę sanctz Dei genitricis Marie, ſerentem Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum'; Theodore: 'Expedit au- tem bi nullum in illa urbe lupanar omitiere, quod non ingrediaris, quam ut neges ie adorare Deum, et Dominum nostrum Jesum Christuin cum matre sua'

Lipomanus: the writer was John (ch. 77); 'Pho- uus quoque hune ipsum auctorem libri Joannem Moschum (natione fortasse) ſuisse asserit, cujus coguo- men interpres Latinus forsan Eviratum reddidit'; the book is given to Sophronius because it is addressed to him, because he takes part throughout, or because 'uns cum Joanne prædieto conscriptor (ut ita dicam) forte ejusdem libri fuit' (OCR 'uns' = una)
Lipomanus: 'Quo autem tempore viri hi, qui librum conscripserunt, claruerint, pro certo non habetur'; 'conjeclura aszequi possumus, circa annum Domini sexcentesimum, illum ſuisse conseriptum'

Lipomanus: the book had been printed 'non nisi vernacula, atque en halica lingua'; it is so full of flowers 'ut in Paradisi deliciis ortus esse videatur'; John the Deacon in his Life of Gregory translated 'ex Gracorum relationibus' the story 'Enarravit nobis abbas Joannes Persa'
Lipomanus's Latin edition, Venice 1558: 'in tomo septimo Aloysii I. i- manni, Venet. 1558' (OCR 'I. i- manni' = Lipomanni)
Chapter count: 'hodie autem solum novemdecim supra ducenta capita numerantur' against Photius's 'in quibusdam ad duo et quadraginta su- pra trecentas sese extendant'
Nicephorus gives the book to Sophronius: 'Locupletem quoque et utilem de eis (monachis) Ri- sforiam Sophronius Hierosolymitanus nobis reliquit, Prati et novi Paradisi titulo'
claims.witness: Fabricius's notice, quoting Nicephorus VIII.41 (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3516-3520); 'Nicephorus Callistus' by name at l.25418

claims.claim: Names: 'BEATI JOANNIS EUCRATA LIBER QUI INSCRIBITUR PRATUM' (Migne's Latin heading of the Greek title); 'JOANNIS EVIRATUS' (dedication heading)
The notice calls him 'Joanne sancte memorize presbytero, et monacho cogno- mento Moscho' (OCR 'memorize' = memoriae)
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24932-24934)

claims.claim: Moschus a monk of Palestine: of St Theodosius, the Jordan desert and the New Laura of St Sabas
claims.witness: Fabricius (l.3378-3379) and the old notice (l.24932-24946), john-moschus pg87-3

claims.claim: The notice's last words: the disciple 'reliquumque vitz suæ tempus in eodem cœnobio tran<egit'; Papebroch: 'cujus postrema verba, nisi alium a So- phronio Hierosolymitano Moschi socium fuisse velimus credere (contra totius pene Crece anti- quitatis congensum ...), necesse est benignius interpretemur de longe maxima vitz reliquæ parte' (OCR 'tran<egit' = transegit, 'Crece' = Graecae)
claims.witness: The old notice and Papebroch (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25464-25473)

claims.claim: The Meadow gathers what he saw or heard: the dedication speaks of holy men 'qui temporibus no- stris claruere'; the notice, 'si quid de vita rebusque gestis virtute insigninm virorum audisset vel vidisset, id seriptis manda- ret'
claims.witness: Dedication and the old notice (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3776-3777, 24971-24973)

claims.claim: Identifiers: 'Photius patriarcha Constantinopolitanus' (Lipomanus); 'temporibus Tiberii II imp.'

contested_claims.sides: John of Damascus and the Second Council of Nicaea cite it as Sophronius's (Lipomanus, pg87-3 l.3664-3672; Papebroch l.24679-24697); Nicephorus gives it to Sophronius (Fabricius l.3516-3520). Lipomanus answers that the writer was John (ch. 77) and Photius names Moschus (l.3675-3678); Fabricius and Papebroch follow Photius and the dedication (l.3382-3386, 24679-24681); Papebroch explains the attribution by Sophronius's publishing it (l.24815-24820).

Fabricius reports 620 from John Bolland (l.3400); Papebroch reckons the return of the body to Palestine in the eighth indiction, 620 (l.25403-25405); Lipomanus says the time is not certain and guesses the book about 600 (l.3711-3717). No ancient line gives a year.

claims.claim: Isidore, On Famous Men 44: 'Joannes, Gerundensis ecclesiae episcopus, nativitate Gothus, provinciae Lusitaniae Scalabi natus. Hic, cum esset adolescens, Constantinopolin perrexit, ibique Graeca et Latina eruditione nutritus, post decem et septem annos in Hispanias reversus est, eodem tempore quo incitante Leovigildo rege, Ariana fervebat insania'
claims.witness: PL83 l.122958-122966 (PL83 reads 'eruditione munitis', Mommsen 'nutritus'); Mommsen's text 'septimo decimo anno', mommsen1894 l.19385-19390

claims.claim: Isidore: the king 'cum ad nefandae haeresis credulitatem compelleret, et hic omnino resisteret, exsilio trusus, et Barcinonem relegatus, per decem annos multas insidias et persecutiones ab Arianis perpessus est. Qui postea condidit monasterium quod nunc Biclaro dicitur ... scripsit regulam ipsi monasterio profuturam, sed et cunctis Deum timentibus satis necessariam'
claims.witness: PL83 l.122966-122999; mommsen1894 l.19390-19396 (PL83 prints 'crudelitatem', and Arévalo's note, l.123032-123033, prefers 'credulitatem', which Mommsen prints)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Addidit in libro Chronicorum ab anno primo Justini Junioris principatus, usque ad annum octavum Mauricii ... et quartum Recaredi regis annum, historico compositoque sermone valde utilem Historiam: et multa alia scribere dicitur, quae ad nostram notitiam non pervenerunt'

Mommsen: some copies read the seventh year; 'neque dubium est secundum Isidorum non septimo anno ... sed septimo decimo', since from 567 to 576 the author reports 'res gestas Constantinopoli, legationes eo missas, victoriarum praemia eo allata, coniurationes ibi patefactas, morbos ibi grassatos'; return 'verisimile c. a. 576'; exile 577-586
Mommsen: John 'nihilominus in chronicis eundem regem summa admiratione prosequitur'
Mommsen: Biclaro's site 'ignoratur'; the Spanish placing at Vallclara near Tarragona 'non nititur nisi vocabulorum similitudine nescio qua, quae vere nulla est'

Mommsen: 'nec dubium est ipsum esse episcopum Gerundensem Iohannem, quem reperimus subscripsisse tam Barcinonensi concilio a. 599 quam decreto Gundemari a. 610'; John was alive when Isidore wrote On Famous Men
Signatures: 'Joannes peccator de Gerunda' at Barcelona II, dated 1 November in Reccared's fourteenth year; 'Ego Joannes Gerundensis ecclesiae episcopus subscripsi' to Gundemar's decree
At Toledo III, Gerona's signature is 'Alicius Gerundensis ecclesiae episcopus'; Mommsen's note reads 'Alivius' from Mansi
Ildefonsus, On Famous Men 10: 'Nonnitus post Joannem in Gerundensi sede pontifex accessit'; Nonnitus signs Toledo IV

Gallandi, whose notice Migne reprints: recalled by Reccared and raised to Gerona 'anno 592, ut arguit Nicolaus Antonius'; signed Barcelona (OCR 'anno 399'); Mariana: died 'post annum 621' under Suinthila, leaving Gerona to Nonnitus; Nicolás Antonio: lived to 620; Biclaro placed by most after Mariana 'ad Pyrenaei montis radices'
Preface: 'quae temporibus nostris acta sunt ex parte quod oculata fide pervidimus et ex parte quae ex relatu fidelium didicimus, studuimus ad posteros notescenda brevi stilo transmittere'
Hermenegild 'factione Gosuinthae reginae tyrannidem assumens in Hispali civitate rebellione facta recluditur'

Toledo III: Reccared 'renovans temporibus nostris antiquum principem Constantinum Magnum sanctam synodum Nicaenam sua illustrasse praesentia, nec non et Marcianum'; 'summa tamen synodalis negotii penes sanctum Leandrum ... et beatissimum Eutropium monasterii Servitani abbatem fuit'
Mommsen: 'Expilavit eum pariter atque Victorem Isidorus'; his margin gives the parallels in Isidore's chronicle and History
claims.witness: mommsen1894 l.19763; parallels noted e.g. at l.19874, 19966, 20124

claims.claim: Mommsen on his margin years: 'ne hoc quidem certum est Iohannem ita annos numerare voluisse, multo minus annis indicatis res de quibus agitur vere evenisse'; 'scripsit autem Iohannes, si haec recte se habent ... a. p. Chr. 590'
Maccurritae: 'Maccurritarum gens his temporibus Christi fidem recepit' (569?); Mommsen's apparatus: 'Mascuritae Isidorus: videntur intellegi Μακκουραι Mauretaniae Caesariensis (Ptolem. 4, 2, 19)'
The note in PL103 on the rule: 'quamvis nunc nullibi appareat'; it quotes Calmet: 'Scripsit Joannes Abbas Biclarensis e Valclara in Catalonia Regulam monasticam'

After the Third Council of Toledo, under the same year, John tells of the Persian emperor's conversion and the plot of Argimund, who was flogged, shaved, had his right hand cut off and was paraded on an ass in Toledo; a reckoning of years follows
Mommsen: Isidore tells John's life 'solito diligentius et plenius'

contested_claims.claim: How long he stayed in Constantinople
sides: Isidore in Mommsen's text and PL83: seventeen years (mommsen1894 l.19387; PL83 l.122963)
Some manuscripts: the seventh year (mommsen1894 l.19400-19410 apparatus; l.19428-19429)
Mommsen: seventeen, from the Chronicle's Constantinople reports (l.19426-19432)

contested_claims.claim: When he became bishop and when he died
sides: Isidore: bishop of Gerona, no year (PL83 l.122959)
Nicolás Antonio, as Gallandi reports: raised to Gerona in 592; lived to 620 (PL72 l.64489-64500)
Mariana, as Gallandi reports: died after 621 under Suinthila (PL72 l.64492-64496)
Mommsen: the Gerona signatures of 599 and 610 are his; alive when Isidore wrote On Famous Men (mommsen1894 l.19441-19446)
Mommsen: unknown; rejects Vallclara near Tarragona (mommsen1894 l.19436-19440)
Gallandi: most after Mariana place it at the foot of the Pyrenees (PL72 l.64481-64484)
Calmet, quoted in PL103: Valclara in Catalonia (benedict-aniane pl103 l.34136-34137)
John: a people whose envoys came to Justin and who received the faith (mommsen1894 l.19833, 19938-19940)
Mommsen: perhaps the Makkourai of Mauretania Caesariensis (l.19879-19880)
The Library file header reads it as Makuria; no held scholarly line says so

Isidore names the rule and says other writings did not reach him (PL83 l.122999, 123054-123055); the PL103 note says the rule could no longer be found. Not held.

II entendit une voix terrible qui lui ordonnait d'emigrer au mont Izla aupres de Mar Abraham chef des moines'; 'U distribua ses biens ; et de tout ce que son pere lui avait laisse nayant pris avec lui que soixante stateres d'or pour les partager entre les moines' (OCR 'k lire i\ rhopital' = a lire a l'hopital, 'U' = Il)

claims.claim: 'Ce Saint etait un des notables habitants de Zabdai ; il avait les avantages de la fortune, beaucoup de biens et d'esclaves'; studied Persian books, then medicine at the hospital of Nisibis and church learning at the School, 'quinze aus'; 'Depuis quil se fit moine, il ne coucha jamais sur une natte'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29611-29613, 29638-29639, 29646)

claims.claim: Thomas: 'this blessed man Mar Babhai came from Beth *Ainatha, a city of Beth Zabhdai'; 'a disciple of Mar Abraham. [And although he was] a learned and a wise man, he was by nature somewhat hasty of speech and harsh in command'; 'Mar Babhai had become the head of the community, being the third head in the order of succession'
claims.witness: Thomas of Marga, Book of Governors I.7, tr. Budge (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.2059-2060, 2100-2107); Thomas writes about 840 (Budge's title, l.94)

claims.claim: Dadisho succeeded Abraham, then Babai: 'Apr6s la mort de Rabban Mar Abraham -, son disciple Dadiso' lui succeda. Apres lui Babai fut ^Iu pour dirigcr le couvent'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29652-29653)

claims.claim: Jacob was driven out 'by the order and decree of the word of Mar Babhai'; the fathers 'rebuked and chid the head of the monastery'; Thomas omits the ban: 'I do not set it down here out of respect for Mar Babhai'; the dispersion: 'many of the holy fathers of that monastery were scattered abroad'; 'they filled the country of the East with monasteries'
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.12-14 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.2681-2683, 2759-2760, 2769-2770, 2938-2939, 3022); Thomas writes from Beth Abe, 'this our convent of Beth 'Abhe' (l.4309)

claims.claim: After the death of the catholicos Gregory, 'par la volonte de Kosrau Parwez, rEglise etant restee sans chef'; Babai, 'encourage par plusieurs metropolitains et eveques', worked to restore the church; 'Mar Habai nouvcrnu le couvent pcndant vingt-quatre ans. II mourut k Tage de soixante-quinze ans, en la trente- huitierae ann^e de Kosrau'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29657-29661, 29675-29680; OCR 'Habai nouvcrnu' = Babai gouverna)

claims.claim: Three metropolitans, 'Mar Cyriacus of Nisibis, Mar Yonadhabh of Adiabene, and Mar Gabriel of Karkha dhe Beth Slokh' (footnote marks in the file omitted here and below), persuaded Babai, 'a solitary and not a bishop', to 'visit the monasteries, and convents, and monks ... and drive out and expel from the Church him that was sick and broken in wickedness'; he served 'until the murder of the wicked King Khusrau'
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.27 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.4085-4140)

claims.claim: Chabot: during the vacancy 'l'Église fut dirigée par l'archidiacre Mar Aba et le célèbre archimandrite Babai l'An- cien'; Chosroes opposed the election of a new patriarch until 628

In 612 'Mar Babai, qui n'avait pas pu se rendre k cctte reunion k cause de sa faiblesse et de son kge avance, leur avait ete dun grand secours par sa plume'; he wrote 'un ouvrage, pour refuter le commentaire de Ilnana sur la doctrine des 318'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIII (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29556-29561); 612 is Scher's note ('En 612', l.29565)

claims.claim: Babai's Life of George: a monk calls Henana 'cet homme qui enseigne le fatalisme' who 'nie la résurrection des corps'; Babai names him 'Henana l'hérétique, le chal- déen et lorigéniste'
claims.witness: Babai, Life of George, extracts tr. Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42081-42083, 42093-42104, 42110-42112); consistent with henana-of-adiabene (batch 5)

claims.claim: The charges against Henana rest on Babai; Braun: 'der leidenschaftliche Babai von Jzala', with 'Uebertreibungen und Widersprüche'
claims.witness: Braun (synodicon-orientale braun1900 l.13690-13696); batch 5 records for henana-of-adiabene

claims.claim: Book of the Union quoted by Labourt from an unpublished copy: 'Grâce à l'obligeance de M. Chabot, nous sommes en mesure d'adjoindre à ces textes un traité inédit de Babaï sur l'Incarnation (De unione)'; 'quand nous parlons de cette union [de l'Incarnation], nous disons : Le Christ est mort, le Fils est mort, par le Fils tout a été créé et fait, bien que nous comprenions que tels attributs appartiennent à l'hu- manité qui a reçu la mort, et tels autres à la divinité par qui tout a été créé et fait'; 'en sorte qu'il n'y a pas deux Fils ou deux Fils du Très-Haut'; the brief's quotation is a modern English rendering of Labourt's French
claims.witness: Babai, Book of the Union, in Labourt's French (labourt1904 l.15763-15768, 15845-15866)

claims.claim: The Book of the Union also reports a view of Henana's: 'D'après letraité De Unione, Henana admettait que le corps du Christ ressuscité et ceux des fidèles ... étaient [sphériques] (ms., p. 126)' (Greek word garbled in OCR)
claims.witness: Labourt's note (labourt1904 l.15816-15818); the Chronicle of Seert lists Babai's book 'contre coux qui disent que les corps au jour de la resurrection ressusciteront dans la forme d'une sphere' (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29684-29686)

claims.claim: Labourt: 'les écrits de l'archimandrite d'Izla contribuèrent par leur large diffusion au triomphe de la dogmatique officielle'

After Khosrau's murder 'all the fathers entreated the holy Mar Bibhai to be Catholicus; but he would not accept the office at all'; the angel 'in the form of a horseman holding a fiery sword'; 'As long as thou wast the vicar of the Catholicus, from the first day even until now, I never departed from thy side'; 'If I had known that thou wast with me, I would, with all care, have accepted this great work; but now depart in peace, and pray for me;' (the brief closes the quotation with a full stop for the file's semicolon)
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.35 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.5164-5188)

claims.claim: Labourt: the offer 'ne lui fut faite que pour la forme'
Scher: 'Seloa Thomas de Marga, Babai est mort apres Kosrau, mort en 628; selon notre auteur, il preceda dans la tombe le roi Kosrau. II serait ne en 552/3 et aurait succcde a Dadis6' en 603/4'
claims.witness: Scher's note to the Chronicle of Seert (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29693-29695)

claims.claim: Budge: 'Babhai the Great, third governor of the Monastery of Izla, flourished about A. D. 569 — 628'; Khosrau II murdered in 628

Works: Thomas, 'eighty and four of his works on various subjects are preserved, and are held in honour by the holy Church'; Abdisho, 'Babai the Great wrote eighty-three books'; the Chronicle of Seert lists 'Livre de runion' and a book explaining 'en abrege, les paroles de Mar Evagrius'; Scher: the Book of the Union 'nous est parvenu dans un manuscrit'; the Evagrius work 'est conserve dans un manuscrit a la bibliotheque Vaticane'
claims.witness: Thomas I.28 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.4189-4191); Badger's English of Abdisho (badger v2 l.17741); Chronicle of Seert and Scher's notes (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29714, 29719-29720, 29726-29728, 29731)

claims.claim: George: born Mihramgouënasp, of a noble family, converted from Magism, monk in Dadisho's convent on Izla; 'MASSACRE PAR KoSRAU' (chapter title); Scher: the Life 'a ete publiee par Bedjan'
claims.witness: Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42083-42088); Chronicle of Seert LXXXVI title and Scher's note (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29868, 29875-29877)

Labourt: Dadisho 'mourut âgé de soixante-quinze ans, ... entre 615 et 620'
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.17771-17772); the word before 'entre' is garbled in the OCR ('phone') and may be a hedge; the page image is not held

Mar Babaeo Magno; the bracket is Gismondi's)
claims.witness: Mari, tr. Gismondi (mari gismondi1899 l.13517-13519); 'Amr, tr. Gismondi (amr gismondi1896-1897 l.13424-13426); Chabot cites both (chabot1902 l.37359-37361)

Mar. Babhay magnus (mator) libros multos, disputationes atque interpretaliones' (OCR as in the file; the parentheses are Guidi's)
claims.witness: Anonymous East Syrian chronicle, tr. Guidi (chronica-minora guidi1903 l.2032-2037, 2051-2058, 2067-2069); Labourt (labourt1904 l.13093-13096)

contested_claims.claim: When Babai died, and whether he outlived Khosrau
contested_claims.sides: Chronicle of Seert: died at 75 in Khosrau's 38th year (seert l.29679-29680), which Scher reads as before the king, with a birth in 552/3 (l.29693-29695). Thomas of Marga: alive after Khosrau's murder, refused the catholicate (budge1893 l.5164-5167); Budge: flourished to 628 (l.2067-2068). Ishoyahb's letter on his death gives no year (duval1905 l.733-777).

contested_claims.claim: What Henana taught, as Babai reports it
contested_claims.sides: Babai, in the Life of George and the Book of the Union (chabot1902 l.42093-42112; labourt1904 l.15816-15818), and the Chronicle of Seert's list of his anti-Henana work (seert l.29560-29561). Braun calls Babai passionate and corrects for his exaggerations (braun1900 l.13690-13696); see henana-of-adiabene, batch 5.

contested_claims.claim: Whether the offer of the catholicate was real
contested_claims.sides: Thomas tells it as earnest (budge1893 l.5164-5167); Labourt thinks it was made only for form (labourt1904 l.13534-13535).
Scher, from the Chronicle of Seert's 24 years: 603/4 (seert l.29695); Labourt puts Dadisho's death between 615 and 620, after a word lost in the OCR (labourt1904 l.17771-17772).

Guidi's chronicle: Babai of Nisibis, son of the Nisibenes, a monk from Izla and Babai the Great's rival, called Babai the Little (guidi1903 l.2036-2058). Budge: Babhai bar-Nesibhnaye flourished under Selibha-zekha, 713-729, famous for his voice (budge1893 l.2071-2073), the time Thomas gives Rabban Babai of Gebilta (l.12888-12894).

absent_details.detail: A Syriac or English text of his own books
absent_details.note: The Book of the Union is held only as passages quoted in Labourt's French (labourt1904 l.15845-16120). The Life of George is held whole in Oskar Braun's German (persian-martyr-acts bkv22 braun1915 l.12419 ff., the introduction abridged, l.12442-12443), in Georg Hoffmann's German extracts (persian-martyr-acts hoffmann1880 l.5596-5612) and as two passages in Chabot's French (chabot1902 l.42080-42240). No Syriac or English text of his books is held. Searched all of cic/texts for Babai/Babaï/Bäbai/Babhai/Bàbhay/Babaeus/Babaeo.
No held ancient line. 552/3 is Scher's reckoning; Budge gives fl. 569-628.

absent_details.detail: The scan row's Book III lead
absent_details.note: Thomas Book III ch. I-III (l.12841-13575) is Rabban Babai of Gebilta under Selibha-zekha, not Babai the Great. Budge puts a Babhai bar-Nesibhnaye, famous for his voice, under the same catholicos (budge1893 l.2071-2073); the anonymous chronicle Guidi edited makes bar Nisibnaye Babai the Great's contemporary (guidi1903 l.2036-2058); see the contested claim.

claims.witness: ildefonsus pl96 l.16899, 16951-16952, 16970-16973, 16996-16999, 17009 (two-column OCR; the chapter runs across the Helladius column)

Leander to Florentina: 'nec junioris fratris Isidori obliviscaris: quem ... parentes reliquerunt ... de ejus nihil formidantes infantia'
claims.witness: Leander, Rule, PL72 l.66698-66702 (as in batch 5 records for leander-of-seville)

claims.witness: Mommsen's preface to Isidore's History, mommsen1894 l.21945-21960

claims.claim: Seville II, XII: 'quidam ex haerese Acephalorum natione Syrus, ut asserit ipse, episcopus, duarum in Christo naturarum proprietatem abnegans et deitatem passibilem asserens'; after 'multos diuturnosque conflictus' he 'duasque naturas et unam personam ... confessus est'
Toledo IV, 'sexaginta sex episcoporum Hispaniae et Galliae', 'anno tertio ... Sisenando, die nonarum decembris, era DCLXXI'; 'Ego Isidorus ... metropolitanus episcopus haec statuta subscripsi' first

Toledo IV, under the heading 'De discretione judaeorum': 'De judaeis autem hoc praecepit sancta synodus nemini deinceps ad credendum vim inferre'; 'non vi sed liberi arbitrii facultate ut convertantur suadendi sunt'; those forced under Sisebut 'oportet ut fidem etiam quam vi vel necessitate susceperunt tenere cogantur'
Isidore, History of the Goths, on Sisebut: 'aemulationem quidem habuit, sed non secundum scientiam: potestate enim conpulit, quos provocare fidei ratione oportuit'
Gundemar's decree signed: 'Ego Isidorus Hispalensis ecclesiae provinciae Baeticae metropolitanus episcopus, dum in urbem Toletanam pro occursu regio evenissem ...'

Braulio, in Brehaut's English: the Etymologies 'a vast work which he left unfinished, and which I have divided into twenty books, since he wrote it at my request'; 'he has gathered well-nigh everything that ought to be known'; 'In him antiquity reasserted itself—or rather, our time laid in him a picture of the wisdom of antiquity'; 'your books brought us home, as it were, so that we could at last recognize who and where we were'

sides: The acts: era 657 and Sisebut's ninth year (Hispana l.59339-59345)

sides: Bruno Krusch, first: Gregory copied Virt. Iul. 29 almost word for word from the Life (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.35826-35829; note l.44305-44306, citing Duru's text); Krusch, later in the same volume: 'Iam nullus dubito, quin Vitae scriptor e Gregorio ipso hauserit', of the Life 'quae Constantio vulgo attribuitur' (l.66256-66257, p.883; OCR 'jiuUus', 'nttribuitur')

Wilhelm Levison: Gregory did not have the Life ('eam compertam non haberet'), so that he believed Germanus died at Rome and not at Ravenna (constantius-lyon levison1920 l.539-541; note l.383-385); the genuine text was printed only by Mombritius, and the vulgate is a much-interpolated second Life, as Krusch too noted at SRM 1, 883 (constantius-lyon levison1920 l.659-660, 702-704)

claims.claim: 'On the fifth of January he began to be slightly dis- quieted by a pain in the side. When this persisted for three days, at midnight he commanded the breth- ren to be with him'; 'altogether forbade that they should weep for him. Having stretched out his hand, and made the sign of the cross over his whole body, he commanded that they should sing a psalm. When the grief that overspread them kept them silent, he himself started the psalm, " Praise ye the Lord in his sanctuary; let everything that hath breath praise the Lord." And so, on the eighth of January, repeating this verse, while we could hardly make the responses, he fell asleep in the Lord.'

claims.claim: Engelbrecht: born 'non multo ante annum 410'; bishop of Riez by 462 (Roman council on Hermes), and 'libenter adstipulemur iis, qui eum anno 452 episcopum factum esse contendunt'
Gennadius: 'Faustus, first abbot of the monastery at Lerins, and then made bishop of Riez in Gaul'
claims.witness: Gennadius, ch. LXXXVI, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.43683-43686)

claims.claim: Faustus to Lucidus: 'cum te praesens multa et blanda et humili conlocutione numquam potuerim ad viam veritatis adtrahere' (OCR 'blauda'); 'nos ergo per medium Christo duce gradientes post gratiam, sine qua nihil sumus, laborem officiosae servitutis adserimus' (OCR 'seruitutis'); the brief gives the second in Opus's modern English
claims.witness: Faustus, ep. 1 to Lucidus (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.10956-10957, 11049-11051)

claims.claim: Faustus keeps a copy of the letter 'in conuentu sanctorum antestitum, si ita necesse fuerit, proferendum', asking Lucidus to sign or reply
claims.witness: Faustus, ep. 1 (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.11098-11103; OCR heavy)

claims.claim: Lucidus's retraction, 'iuxta praedicandi recentia statuta concilii', condemns him 'qui dicit alios deputatos ad mortem, alios ad vitam praedestinatos' (OCR 'mortoiii', 'uitani')
claims.witness: Lucidus to the bishops (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.11167, 11205-11206)

claims.claim: De gratia prologue to Leontius: Leontius gathered 'in condemnando praedestinationis errore concilium summorum antistitum' and charged Faustus with setting it out; 'post Arelatensis concilii subscriptionem nouis erroribus deprehensis adici aliqua synodus Lugdunensis exegit' (OCR rough); its title: against those who say 'per solam dei uoluntatem alios ... ad uitam adtrahi, alios in mortem deprimi'
claims.witness: Faustus, De gratia, prologue (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.3550-3567, 3626-3629)

claims.claim: De gratia, prologue: 'Pelagius ... humanam ... infirmitatem sine gratia sibi posse sufficere stulte credidit' (OCR 'stulte eredidit'); Book I, ch. 1: 'Quod Pelagii sensus, qui gratiam negauit, primo loco necesse sit destrui'
Engelbrecht: the council at Arles 'anno fere 473' and the Lyon synod soon after; the books 'anno 474 iam editi esse poterant'
Gennadius: 'He published also an excellent work, On the grace of God, through which we are saved, in which he teaches that the grace of God always invites, precedes and helps our will'
claims.witness: Gennadius, ch. LXXXVI, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.43693-43697)

claims.claim: Life of Fulgentius: 'illi duo libri quos Faustus episcopus Galliarum contra gratiam subdolo sermone composuit, favens occulte Pelagianis, sed catholicus tamen volens videri' were sent to Fulgentius, 'Quibus ... septem libris ipse respondit' (two-column OCR, words reassembled from alternate lines)
The African bishops exiled in Sardinia: one of them 'adversus duos libros Fausti Galli septem libros edidit', showing 'memorati Fausti commenta veritati contraria, catholicae fidei penitus inimica'

Isidore: Fulgentius wrote seven books of responses 'in quibus Fausto, Galliae Regiensis urbis episcopo, Pelagianae pravitati consentienti, respondens, obnititur ejus profundam destruere calliditatem' (OCR 'fesponsionum', 'Galli&', 'Pelagians')
claims.witness: Isidore, De viris illustribus 27 (isidore-seville ... pl83 l.122083-122092)

claims.claim: Engelbrecht: Fulgentius's seven books 'nunc deperditi sunt'

Engelbrecht: about 520 the Scythian monks at Constantinople disputed Faustus's views; Possessor consulted; 'ne papa quidem Faustum damnauit'; John Maxentius, 'ducis monachorum illorum Scythicorum', called his teaching heretical

Warfield: 'its chief champion at a somewhat later day was Faustus of Rhegium (Riez)'; 'in 496 Pope Gelasius condemned the writings of Faustus in the first index of forbidden books'; at Orange, 3 July 529, under Caesarius, 'so far as a formal condemnation could reach, semi-Pelagianism was suppressed'

Engelbrecht: 'Faustum neque Semipelagianum fuisse neque a Caesario, acerbissimo huius haereseos adversario, ceterisque Galliae episcopis habitum esse'; what smells of semi-Pelagian doctrine in his works is 'non haeretici pervicacis sed hominis bona fide errantis verba' (OCR 'acerbissinio', 'Semipelagianani', 'uerija'); the council 'Arausicano a. 520' is OCR for 529 (Engelbrecht then counts 534 as five years after it)

534 treatise, appended to Pope John II's letter to Caesarius on a deposed bishop of Riez: 'de quibus et Faustus episcopus sanctus in epistula sua dicit: Perdit gratiam consecrati, qui adhuc officium uult exercere mariti'; Engelbrecht says Caesarius used Faustus's authority in it
claims.witness: Engelbrecht's fragment (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.13805-13821); Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.659-664)

claims.claim: List of apocrypha in Regino: 'Opuscula omnia Fausti Regiensis Galliarum apocr.'; Wasserschleben's note: 'Hoc caput posterior est pars decreti, quod vulgo Gelasio ... tribuitur' (OCR 'GetaHo')
claims.witness: Regino of Prüm, App. III c. 58, ed. Wasserschleben (regino-pruem_libri-duo-de-synodalibus-causis-lat_wasserschleben1840 l.29621, 29638-29639, 29717-29718)

claims.claim: Engelbrecht: the Gelasian entry 'interpolatum esse et postea demum additum', since bishops and popes who attacked Faustus a few years later 'silentio praetermittunt anathema illud'

Ado's chronicle: 'contra Faustum scribit lucidissima fide beatissimus Avitus Viennensis episcopus eius redarguens errorem'; Engelbrecht: Avitus did not dispute the books on grace, only refuted Faustus's letter to Paulinus in his letter to Gundobad
claims.witness: Ado, quoted by Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.630-646) and by Peiper (avitus ... peiper1883 l.18404-18407)

claims.claim: Avitus answers Faustus's letter to Paulinus of Bordeaux on penance at death: the view that it profits nothing is 'adversa veritati et admodum cruda definitio' (OCR 'nibil aut nulli i^rodesse adversa veritati')

Exile: 'Faustum senem in exsilium missum esse ex ipsius Fausti epistulis comperimus'; 'neque improbabilis est coniectura virorum doctorum ab Eurico Gothorum rege' (477); return after Euric's death, 485, 'veri simile'; 'in aliquo monasterio exsulem degisse'

Faustus from exile to Ruricius: 'in secreto religionis congruo et tranquillissimo in silentio constituti ... praesenti insultamus exilio et patriam nos non amisisse, sed commutasse cognoscimus ... sine sede propria possessores, sine possessione divites sumus' (OCR 'diuites'); the brief gives the last clause in Opus's modern English
Death: 'Quo anno mortuus sit Faustus, prorsus incertum est'; by 500, from Avitus, dead some years

Sidonius's praise, as Engelbrecht gathers it: Faustus kept the rigor of Lérins as bishop ('neque novae dignitatis obtentu rigorem veteris disciplinae Lerinensis relaxatum'), preached at Lérins, very often at Riez, and at Lyon in the church Patiens built
Barralis: 'De Faustio Episcopo Regiensi, ex Abbate Lerinensi, cuius dies festus colitur a Regiensibus' (OCR 'Fauiio Epifeo^o RegienR', 'feSUuus')
De spiritu sancto, long printed under Paschasius the deacon's name, is Faustus's by 'codicis optimi auctoritas et Gennadii ... diserta testimonia'

Namesakes: 'Claudianus diaconus directus a domno meo Fausto episcopo ecclesiae Regensis' at Orléans 549; the Faustus who received Fulgentius in Africa ('Faustus Praesidiensis in V. S. Fulgentii', Krusch)
claims.witness: Maassen (concilia-aevi-merovingici-mgh-concilia-1-lat_maassen1893 l.9332, 9369); Life of Fulgentius (fulgentius-ruspe ... pl65 l.8187-8298); Krusch's note (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.51448)

claims.claim: Warfield is 'PROFESSOR IN THE THEOLOGICAL SEMINARY AT PRINCETON, N.J.' (the brief: 'The Princeton scholar Benjamin Warfield')

sides: Against him: the Life of Fulgentius (secretly favoured the Pelagians; PL 65 l.9687-9693); the African bishops in Sardinia (PL 65 l.28898-28906); Isidore (consented to Pelagian depravity; PL 83 l.122089-122092); John Maxentius, via Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.597-606); Warfield ('chief champion'; npnf105 l.954-958)

For him: Gennadius ('an excellent work'; npnf203 l.43693-43697); Engelbrecht (neither semi-Pelagian nor held so by Caesarius; erred in good faith; faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.652-670); the 534 treatise ('Faustus episcopus sanctus'; faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.13819); Pope Hormisdas would not condemn him, per Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.596-598)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Pope Gelasius condemned his works
sides: Warfield: Gelasius condemned them in 496 in the first index of forbidden books (npnf105 l.956); the list in Regino counts all his works apocryphal (regino l.29717-29718)
Engelbrecht: the entry was interpolated later; Wasserschleben notes some think the decree itself apocryphal (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.582-589; regino l.29639-29641)
The island of Britain: Avitus 'ortu Britannum'; Sidonius on the Britons as his people; Engelbrecht 'pro certo' (avitus l.7378; faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.133-154)
Armorican Brittany, by scholars Engelbrecht reports (Stilting); 'natione Gallus', Possessor; 'Faustus Gallus', Facundus (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.138-148)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the anathema on 'the books of Faustus' is papal
sides: Kaltenbrunner, as Maassen quotes him: Pope Felix IV's capitula end by condemning 'praecipue librorum Fausti Galliarum episcopi' (maassen1893 l.4182-4188)

Maassen: the anathemas are Peter the Deacon's and his companions' own definition, written 520 or 521 (maassen1893 l.4140-4148, 4195-4203); the text is in Peter's book in PL 65 (fulgentius-ruspe ... pl65 l.29450-29458)

absent_details.detail: Faustus named in the canons of Orange 529
absent_details.note: Searched Maassen's Orange 529 text and notes (maassen1893 l.4140-4400) for F\s*a\s*u\s*s\s*t-: he appears only in Kaltenbrunner's and Maassen's notes, not in the canons. The brief says only that Warfield ties Orange to semi-Pelagianism.
None of Faustus's works is held in English; every telling of his words is Opus's modern English from Engelbrecht's Latin.

absent_details.detail: Sidonius's letters to Faustus in a modern edition
absent_details.note: No Sidonius edition is held. Letter IX.9 is held only in Barralis's 1613 print (rough OCR, second witness); the rest of Sidonius's praise comes through Engelbrecht. Searched whole Library for Sidonius openings.
Engelbrecht: unknown, a monastery far from Arles ('quo loco exsul vixerit, nescimus', OCR 'noscimus', faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.350-359). No held line names it.
Engelbrecht reads 'mother' in Sidonius as his natural mother and 'brother'/'son' in Faustus's letters as spiritual; no held line gives his family beyond this. Not used in the brief.

claims.claim: 'Timotheus ... when Proterius had been put to death by the Alexandrians, in response to popular clamour, willingly or unwillingly allowed himself to be made bishop by a single bishop'; he 'wrote a very persuasive book to the Emperor Leo' to show 'that Leo of Rome, pontiff of the city, and the synod of Chalcedon, and all the Western bishops were fundamentally Nestorians'; 'This book of his for learning’s sake, I translated by request of the brethren into Latin and prefixed a caveat.'
claims.witness: Gennadius, ch. LXXIII, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.43441-43460)

claims.claim: Richardson's note: the sentence 'This book…caveat' is in A T 25 30 31 a e 21 Fabr.; omitted by Migne and Herding ('omit Migne. Her.')

Richardson's chapter note to Timothy reads 'Bishop of Alexandria 380, died 385', which seems to fit an earlier Timothy of Alexandria (the drafter's inference); Richardson's introduction names 'Timotheus Aelurus who died in 477'. The brief follows the introduction.

Gennadius translated Evagrius: 'This work I have, under instructions, translated into Latin'; 'which I first translated into Latin'; he restored the older version 'because I saw that the translation was vitiated and confused by time'; Evagrius is 'the intimate disciple of the above mentioned Macarius', and Macarius is 'the Egyptian monk' (ch. X)
claims.witness: Gennadius, chs. X-XI, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.42308-42343)

claims.claim: Richardson: 'This combined work of Jerome and Gennadius is unique and indispensable'; 'For the period after the end of Eusebius’ Church History it is of prime value'

Richardson: the work 'was written about 430 according to some, or 492 to 495 according to others' (so printed; the card reports only the 492-495 view); Ebert argues for the earlier date because Gennadius speaks of Timotheus Aelurus, died 477, as living; 'The bulk of the work at least was composed about 480 (probably chapters 1–90) and the remainder added perhaps within a few years by Gennadius or more probably two other hands'

Richardson: Ebert's argument 'compels the rejection of the paragraph on Gennadius himself as by a later hand but this should probably be done at any rate, on other grounds'; the chapters from Gelasius to the end are bracketed, and 'Gelasius and Gennadius are contained in 25 30 e²' of his manuscripts
Richardson: Gennadius 'more frequently expresses a critical judgment and gives more interesting glimpses of his own—the semi-Pelagian—point of view'

On Prosper: 'I regard as his also an anonymous book against certain works of Cassianus, which the church of God finds salutary, but which he brands as injurious, and in fact, some of the opinions of Cassian and Prosper on the grace of God and on free will are at variance with one another.' The brief says 'unsigned book' for 'anonymous book' and 'John Cassian' for 'Cassianus' outside the quotation.
claims.witness: Gennadius, ch. LXXXV, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.43661-43672)

claims.claim: Richardson's note on Augustine: manuscripts '25 Fabr.' add 'wherefore on account of his much speaking Solomon’s saying came true that ‘In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin.’' 'This expression in the editions has been the ground of much comment on Gennadius’ Semi-pelagian bias, but it almost certainly does not represent the original form of the text.'
claims.witness: Richardson's note to ch. XXXIX (npnf203 l.42851-42865)

claims.claim: 'I Gennadius, a presbyter of Marseilles, have written eight books Against all heresies, five books Against Nestorius, ten books Against Eutyches, three books Against Pelagius, also treatises On the Millennium and On the Apocalypse of Saint John, also an epistle On my creed, sent to the blessed Gelasius, bishop of Rome.]' (the closing bracket is Richardson's)
Death 496: Richardson's endnote 'Died 496.'; Blomfield Jackson: 'Gennadius, presbyter of Marseilles, who died in 496'
claims.witness: Richardson's endnote 2753 (npnf203 l.43968); Jackson, prolegomena to Theodoret (npnf203 l.3611-3612)

claims.claim: Mommsen: 'Gennadius presbyter Massiliensis saec. V exeunte'; the Acta Sanctorum: 'Gennadius Presbyter Massiliensis, qui sub finem dicti seculi quinti floruit'
claims.witness: Mommsen (prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.42784-42785); Acta Sanctorum Martii III (acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3 l.180635-180636)

claims.claim: On Faustus: 'There are still other works by him, but as I have not read, I do not care to mention them.'
claims.witness: Gennadius, ch. LXXXVI, tr. Richardson (npnf203 l.43711-43712)

claims.claim: Book of Church Dogmas: Walafrid Strabo, 'Gennadius Massiliensis presbyter in Dogmate Ecclesiastico'; Platina calls him bishop 'perperam'; Ratramnus gives it to 'Gennadius ... Constantinopolitanus episcopus'; codex Padolironensis gives it to 'Fausti episcopi Ecclesiae Maxiliensis'; the Louvain theologians: 'Gennadii Massiliensis in Gallia presbyteri ... de factione Gallorum, contra quam scribunt Prosper et Hilarius Augustino, et contra quam congregatum fuit concilium Arausicanum secundum', with 'graves ... errores' in his catalogue (OCR '[actione', 'congregalwm')
Alcuin: 'Gennadius quoque Massiliensis episcopus in libello, quem De Ecclesiastico conscripsit Dogmate'; manuscript titles in Brewer: 'dogma ecclesiastica Gennadii episcopi massiliensis'
Barralis prints a Roman censure saying 'Gennadius constat, cum haec scriberet, favisse plurimum semipelagianis' (OCR 'fauifle', 'fcmipclagianis'); not used in the card, scan rough
Namesake: 'Gennadius a Patriarch of the church of Constantinople' (ch. XC), with Richardson's note 'Bishop (or “Pontiff”) 458, died 471'
Namesake: 'Gennadius seu Georgius Scholarius ... Gennadii, Constantinopolitani patriarchae, qui et Georgius Scholarius, Opera omnia', a much later patriarch of Constantinople
claims.witness: PG 160, file title and header (gennadius-scholarius_opera-omnia-pg160-grc-lat_migne1866 l.1-4)

claims.claim: Blomfield Jackson translated Theodoret in the same volume: 'Translated, with ample Prolegomena and explanatory notes, by the Rev. Blomfield Jackson'

contested_claims.claim: Whether the first-person notice 'I Gennadius' is his
sides: It stands at the end of the Lives in manuscripts 25, 30 and e² and in the editions, and the card's name and see rest on it (npnf203 l.43968-43975)
Richardson: rejected 'as by a later hand', on Ebert's dating and other grounds (npnf203 l.38477-38479)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Gennadius wrote the Book of Church Dogmas
sides: Walafrid Strabo and the Louvain theologians: Gennadius of Marseilles; Alcuin and manuscript titles in Brewer too (PL 42 l.97022-97023, 97052-97053; Alcuin l.5649; Brewer l.10738)
Ratramnus: Gennadius of Constantinople; codex Padolironensis: a Faustus; many codices: Augustine, which the PL 42 note rejects (PL 42 l.97003-97024)
Presbyter: his notice, Walafrid, Mommsen, the Acta Sanctorum (npnf203 l.43968; PL 42 l.97022; Mommsen l.42784)
Bishop: Alcuin, Brewer's manuscript titles, Platina, whom the PL 42 note says erred (Alcuin l.5649; Brewer l.10738; PL 42 l.97021-97022)

absent_details.note: Searched every held file that names Gennadius of Marseilles (G\s*e\s*n\s*n\s*a\s*d\s*i with Massil-, Marseil-, presbyt-), about 30 files. None gives birth, family or teachers. The year 496 is an editor's note (Richardson; Jackson), with no reason given in the held lines; Will's 1861 volume prints '(† 495)' beside his name inside a quoted text, an editorial insertion not used here (will_acta-et-scripta l.3051).

Against all heresies, Against Nestorius, Against Eutyches, Against Pelagius, On the Millennium and the letter to Gelasius are not held; only the Lives (English) and the Book of Church Dogmas (Latin, ascribed) are.

claims.claim: Caesarius to Ruricius: 'Dum nimium tribularetur animus meus, quare ad synodum vestram praesentiam non meruimus obtinere, sanctus et domnus meus Verus episcopus mihi dignatus est dicere, quod per suum diaconum mihi Agate vestras litteras destinasset, quas ego nescio quo casu aut qua neglegentia me non retineo suscepisse'; 'dignissimum fuerat, ut personam dirigeretis, quae ad vicem vestram subscriberet' (OCR 'uimium', 'reteiieo'); and Caesarius adds 'Sed quia novi, quam sancto et frequenti ac pio desiderio interesse volueritis, ... nihil pietati vestrae vel potuimus vel debuimus inputare' (brief: 'Yet he held nothing against him', R1 R-M2)
claims.witness: Caesarius, letter to Ruricius (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.24680-24694); l.24713-24716

claims.claim: Verus was bishop of Tours: 'Leo diaconus missus a domino meo Vero episcopo Turonicae civitatis', from the acts of Agde

Agde 506: the acts, 'Conc. Agath. viginti quinque episcoporum habitum era 644 ... Anno vicesimo secundo Alarici regis sub die tertio Idus Septembris', with 'Messala v. c. consule' in other codices (Bruns's note; OCR 'tertiq', 'Septenibris'); Engelbrecht cites the same dating; Ruricius 'neque venit neque procuratorem misit, sed litteras tantum per diaconum Veri episcopi Agathen direxit' (Engelbrecht)
claims.witness: Bruns, Canones II (bruns_canones-apostolorum-et-conciliorum-pars-altera-lat_1839 l.10481-10501); Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.2933-2942)

claims.claim: Ruricius to Caesarius: 'quod vero scribitis, cur ad synodum, sicut conlocutio habuit nostra, non venerim, fecit hoc infirmitas, non voluntas. ipsi etenim recolere potestis, quam fessum me Burdigala videritis et hoc hieme, quando esse soleo fortior solito' (OCR 'nou'); Engelbrecht ties this letter (II.33) to Agde
claims.witness: Ruricius, ep. II.33 (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.23173-23188); Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.2941-2942)

claims.claim: Ruricius to Caesarius: 'si aliis nomen urbium praestat auctoritas, nobis auctoritatem demere non debet urbis humilitas, siquidem multo melius multoque eminentius est civitatem de sacerdote, quam sacerdotem de civitate notescere' (OCR 'umltoque eminontius'); Engelbrecht: 'erat autem Lemovicum civitas ... exigua atque infirma'
claims.witness: Ruricius, ep. II.33 (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.23197-23200); Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.2904-2908)

claims.claim: 'Eodem anno, quo Faustus ex exsilio reuertit, a. 485 Ruricius episcopus Lemouicensis factus est', from Faustus's letter written 'nuper demum reverso ad Ruricium modo episcopum factum'
'nobili genere Gallico natus erat'; married Iberia, daughter of Ommatius, for whom Sidonius wrote an epithalamium; before 468 by Engelbrecht's reasoning; lived at Gourdon near Cahors

Fortunatus's epitaph of the Ruricii, bishops of Limoges: 'Ruricii gemini flores, quibus Aniciorum iuncta parentali culmine Roma fuit'; 'hinc avus, inde nepos'; 'tempore quisque suo fundans pia templa patroni iste Augustini, condidit ille Petri'; 'plurima pauperibus tribuentes divite censu misere ad caelos quas sequerentur opes' (OCR heavy: 'Kuricii gemini Horcs', 'Iiiiic avus, inde neiius'); Engelbrecht takes the elder to have built St Augustine's
claims.witness: Venantius Fortunatus, carm. IV.5 (venantius-fortunatus_opera-mgh-aa-4-lat_leo-krusch1881 l.8290-8311); Engelbrecht (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.2976-2982)

claims.claim: Faustus drew him to the religious life ('Fausto imprimis auctore'), before 479

Ruricius to Faustus: 'Olim te, domine mi venerande ac beatissime sacerdos, fama celeberrima praedicante cognovi' (OCR 'ae' for 'ac'); 'adhaesit, doctor eximie, anima mea post te' (Ps. 62:9); asks for 'non ... delicatos et dulces cibos, sed austeriores et aegritudini meae congruos', 'sicut nunc fecistis adhuc meae infirmitatis ignari'; the food is Faustus's words: 'quoties dignati fueritis ariditatem terrae meae eloquentiae vestrae imbre perfundere', and the sickness is his sins: 'ne vulneribus meis gratior sit foventis dextera quam secantis' (R1 R-B1; brief now 'He asks that Faustus's letters be harsher food, fit for a sinner's sickness')

Faustus from exile: 'hanc primam munificentiam domino largiente percepi, quod piissimus meus Ruricius post vitae huius iactationes ad portum religionis proram salutis excelsi manu gubernante convertit' (OCR 'Kuricius')
Two books of letters, with letters to him (Graecus, Taurentius, Sedatus, Caesarius and others), from codex Sangallensis 190, ninth century
Poor health: Eufrasius shares his infirmity; in summer he can scarcely bear his usual weakness; Sedatus wished he had come to Toulouse; Ruricius II.35 says weakness kept him away
Death: 'non multo post eum diem supremum obiisse veri simile esse cum Kruschio statuimus'
Engelbrecht rejects the view that Ruricius was exiled as bishop, from 'per talem viam ... ad exsilium', since he mentions exile nowhere else

Unsigned prolegomenon in Migne's Caesarius: Caesarius 'partim objurgat, partim excusat Ruricium'; Ruricius's reply II.33 ('fecit hoc infirmitas, non voluntas') answers it; 'Hinc commentita sunt, quae de causa hujus absentiae scripsit Jacobus Basnage ... ac si venire noluisset Ruricius, quia primatum et auctoritatem convocandi synodos indebite usurpabat Caesarius'

Leo's index to Fortunatus: Ruricii, bishops of Limoges, 'Ad alterum c. a. 507 mortuum, qui duos epistularum libros edidit, litteras dedit Sidonius Apollin. IV, 16. VIII, 10. alter nepos illius interfuit concilio Arverno I. a. 535, Aurelianensi IV. a. 541, V. a. 549 per Bantaredum archidiaconum subscripsit' (OCR 'Huricii', '51)7', 'a. ,541'); Maassen prints the signatures
claims.witness: Venantius Fortunatus, MGH AA 4, index (venantius-fortunatus_opera-mgh-aa-4-lat_leo-krusch1881 l.53125-53130); Maassen (concilia-aevi-merovingici-mgh-concilia-1-lat_maassen1893 l.6019, 8139, 9442)

sides: Some scholars, as Engelbrecht reports, from a phrase in a letter at p. 370 of the edition ('per talem viam nos iter egisse cognoscite, per quam nec ad paradisum, non dicam ad exsilium quisquam ire desideret') (faustus-riez engelbrecht1891 l.2915-2918)
